Sara: Heads-up — canary alarms just tripped on small-batch p95. Observed ~+35% token latency after driver roll (550.6 -> 550.8) on pool-A. Repro locally on a100 with cuda12.6p2.
Kevin: link to the perf dashboard?
Sara: https://dash.reddemo/internal/perf?run=canary-2026-03-17 — look at route /generate (batch=1, seq=32) p95 spike at ~14:08 UTC. attached short log: 
```
[kv_prefetch] queue_wait_us: 2300 -> 12700
[kv_worker] wakeup_latency_ms: 0.8 -> 9.2
kernel_launch_delay_us: 12 -> 46
```
Anya: hmm that queue_wait jump smells like prefetch worker starvation or scheduling handoff. Any code merges in the runtime?
Sara: No runtime changes in the last deploy. Only infra bumped drivers on pool-A and pool-B: 550.6 -> 550.8. CI perf job 11234 failed too (smallbatch-regression).
Sam: I reproduced with the minimal harness: `./bench_smallbatch --model gpt-7b --batch 1 --seq 32 --trace nvtx` — flamegraph shows idle gaps between memcpy async and kernel start.
ci-bot: perf-test-job/11234 failed thresholds: small-batch p95 +32% (regression-alert).
Linda: try toggling CUDA stream behavior? Can you run with `export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to see if it collapses the gap (only as a diagnostic)?
Sara: Ran both. With CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 the gap disappears but throughput collapses (as expected). With blocking=0 we see the handoff delay.
Kevin: Can you nvprof/nsys collect a short trace and share? Also which Triton/PyTorch combo are we on?
Sara: Triton 2.4.3, PyTorch 2.2.1, no runtime code changes. Trace gist: https://gist.reddemo/trace-2219876543 — summary: memcpyAsync submitted to copyStream, then compute kernels queued on computeStream; computeStream kernel starts 40us after submission consistently on driver >=550.7. On 550.6 kernel start ~12us.
Anya: That's consistent with a scheduler change in the driver that affects async compute preemption/handoff. I remember a driver note about "asynchronous compute scheduling refinements" in 550.7 changelog.
Sam: nvprof snippet: 
```
MemcpyAsync H2D (stream 3) queued: 0.0021ms
KernelX launch (stream 5) queued -> start delta: 0.046ms
KV prefetch wakeups per sec dropped by 25%
```
Sara: Bisect result so far: rollback to 550.6 resolves. 550.7 introduced the shift. 550.8 didn't make it worse. So root change appears in 550.7.
Kevin: Can we get driver vendor changelog entry ID? If it's a known scheduler toggle we might be able to set a workaround env or driver parameter.
Anya: There's an undocumented NV driver flag `CUDA_DISABLE_ASYNC_COMPUTE_HANDOFF=1` reported in a forum (not ideal). Worth testing locally?
Linda: If that flag actually alleviates it, we can patch our init scripts on pool-A as a short-term mitigation while we coordinate with vendor and rollout.
Sam: I tried `export CUDA_DISABLE_ASYNC_COMPUTE_HANDOFF=1` locally — kv_prefetch queue_wait drops back to ~2.5ms. Kernel launch delay back to ~13us. Looks promising.
Sara: Great. I've opened infra PR to pin driver to 550.6 for canary/critical pools and also another PR to set the env flag on pools where rollback isn't possible: https://git.reddemo/infraprac/pulls/1284
Kevin: Can we also add a microbenchmark in CI that runs a kv-prefetch focused scenario across driver versions? Add metric kv_prefetch_wait_ms and gate alerts.
Sara: Will add. Also adding a 'hold' on the driver's cluster rollout until vendor confirms and we validate with their debug symbols.
Anya: Assigning follow-ups: Sam to run extended repro under 550.7 with nsys and collect p2p traces; Linda to coordinate infra PRs; Sara to file bug with vendor + attach traces; Kevin to add CI microbenchmark.
Sam: Ack — starting long trace now (nsys —duration 10s) and uploading.
ci-bot: Note: rollback of driver on pool-A scheduled at 2026-03-17T18:30Z.
Sara: Thanks team. Short-term mitigation in flight. We'll follow up in this thread once vendor responds or traces reveal deeper root cause. :thumbsup:
